title: Sweaty Soccer Stars: Why the 2026 World Cup Might Be the Hottest Ever
summary: Have you ever run around on a scorching day and felt like you were melting? Now imagine doing that in front of millions of fans at the World Cup! That's what soccer players might face in 2026. Scientists say this could be the hottest World Cup ever, with about one in four games played in very hot conditions. Last week, photos showed European players, who aren't used to such heat, lying on the field and pouring water over themselves to cool off. Norway's team even wore ice collars around their necks during a game! But England's captain, Harry Kane, says the heat won't be a problem because his team is training hard. So, what's really going on? Climate experts say the world is getting warmer, and many World Cup stadiums are in places like Dallas, Houston, and Miami, where summer days often hit 28°C (about 82°F). Some stadiums have air conditioning, but not all. The heat can make players sweat so much that they get tired, cramp up, or even feel dizzy. But coaches say good training can help. In fact, some teams from hot countries might even have a tiny advantage! So, will the heat be a game-changer? We'll have to watch and see—just maybe with an ice-cold drink in hand.
why_it_matters: If you play sports on hot days, you know how tough it is to keep your energy up—just like these top athletes!
